response.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) AS avg_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-') AND p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA = '-') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY (AVG(l.HCT) IS NULL), AVG(l.HCT) DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: A patient qualifies if they have at least one lab record with U-PRO = '-' and at least one lab record (possibly a different date) with RA = '-'. The averages then cover all of that patient's lab records, not just the qualifying ones.

alternatives.interpretation: Both tests must be '-' in the same lab record. Patients qualify if some single record has U-PRO = '-' and RA = '-'. Averages still cover all of their lab records.
